operations_plan.summary: Identify the intended coffee-pot handle, calculate its interference with the coffee-pot body, and construct temporary exact-fit and clearance envelopes. Interpret "handle" as the front pull handle F-12 rather than the external U-shaped cradle F-18.

steps.description: Isolate the front brewing vessel assembly and verify the target pair by topology and proximity. Treat F-12 (front pull handle, nominally solid 7) as the editable handle and F-13/F-14 (outer vessel and nested liner, nominally solids 8 and 9) as the coffee-pot reference. Confirm that F-12 terminates at or intersects the exterior of F-13 and that the reported collision is not between the main enclosure and the external cradle F-18. This resolves the wording ambiguity in favor of the handle directly associated with the removable coffee pot; if solid-to-feature mapping differs from the nominal ordering, identify the solids from faces 252-258 and 259-280 before continuing.

Run a precise B-rep common/interference calculation between the handle solid and the coffee-pot solids. Record every positive-volume intersection and its connected components. Use the main outer cylindrical vessel face 264, adjacent rim/shoulder faces 259-263 and 265-274, and the liner faces 275-280 only where exposed to the handle. Also calculate the closest-distance field between the handle faces 252-258 and these pot faces so that near-contact regions are included in the clearance correction.

Identify the intentional mounting lands at the terminal regions where the handle joins the pot. Derive these lands from the connected portions of rear attachment face 258 that are necessary to keep the handle attached to F-13; classify the remaining handle-to-pot proximity as unintended interference. The exact mount boundaries are not explicitly supplied and are therefore an unresolved reference to be inferred from topology, symmetry, and load-path continuity. Preserve face contact at the mounting lands but do not preserve positive-volume penetration.

Create two temporary construction bodies from the coffee-pot exterior. First, copy the exact exterior boundary of F-13, supplemented by any exposed F-14 surfaces, to form an exact interference-trimming tool. Second, offset the same exterior outward by a small positive clearance parameter c and form a closed clearance-envelope tool. Exclude the intentional mounting-land footprints from the offset portion so those footprints may end in conformal face contact. No clearance value or model unit is stated in the request; define c as a configurable manufacturing-clearance parameter, using the project standard when available and otherwise a provisional 0.5 mm only after confirming that the model is millimetric and that this value is small relative to the handle thickness.

operations_plan.summary: Remove positive-volume penetration and locally reprofile the front pull handle to provide nonzero clearance from the coffee pot while retaining conformal mounting contact and the existing grip.

steps.description: Boolean-subtract the exact coffee-pot trimming tool from F-12. This removes all positive-volume overlap, including overlap at the mounting lands, and replaces it with conformal mating boundaries derived from the vessel exterior. Apply the cut only to the handle solid; do not alter F-13 or F-14. Retain the portions of rear attachment face 258 that lie outside the collision volume and generate new conformal attachment faces where the cut reaches the selected mounting lands.

Boolean-subtract the offset clearance envelope from the non-mounting portions of F-12. Limit the operation with the mounting-land masks from OP-01-ST-03 so that all free handle surfaces have a minimum separation of c while the intentional mounts remain at zero-clearance face contact. Preserve the visible front face 257, the main rounded grip surface 256, the usable finger opening, and the overall handle placement as far as possible; remove only the material needed to clear the pot.

If the Boolean cuts create narrow slivers, disconnected fragments, or impractically thin handle walls, replace only the affected rear handle region with a constrained local loft or boundary surface. Use the c-offset pot surface as the inner limiting profile, connect it tangentially to unchanged handle side walls 252 and 255, and terminate it at the preserved mounting lands. Keep the front grip face 257 and rounded grip face 256 fixed. Thicken or close the replacement surface to recover one watertight handle solid, then repeat the exact and offset cuts to guarantee that the rebuilt region does not re-enter the prohibited envelope.

Finish the new transition edges with tangent fillets or blends whose radii are taken from the adjacent existing rounded handle transitions, particularly faces 254 and 256. Reduce the inherited radius only where required by local wall thickness. Perform a final subtraction with the clearance envelope after blending so no fillet enters the required clearance zone. Do not add edge treatment to the conformal mounting faces where it would reduce the intended bearing area.

operations_plan.summary: Validate that the edited handle is collision-free, remains usable and attached, and has not changed any preserved appliance geometry.

steps.description: Recompute B-rep intersections between the edited F-12 and F-13/F-14. Require zero positive intersection volume everywhere. At the intentional mounting lands, permit coincident mating faces but no volumetric penetration. Outside those lands, require the measured minimum handle-to-pot distance to be at least c within numerical modeling tolerance.

Validate handle integrity and function. Confirm that F-12 is one watertight solid, remains connected to both intended mounting regions, retains a continuous load path into the pot, has no sub-tolerance walls or knife edges, and preserves the original grip opening and accessible front gripping surfaces 256 and 257. Compare the unchanged portions of the handle with the original geometry to ensure that modification is localized to the interference region.

Verify preservation of the rest of the assembly by comparing all non-handle solids to their pre-edit B-reps and transforms. In particular, keep the coffee-pot body and liner, enclosure SEC-01, front plates SEC-03, feet SEC-05, external cradle SEC-06, and power connection SEC-07 unchanged. Delete the temporary trimming and clearance construction bodies after successful validation and regenerate the multiview assembly to visually confirm separation between the handle and pot.
